title: Follow one MR1 cable
intro: Pick a cable. Match its label at both ends, then compare the named functions. Work deenergized; these routes do not approve energizing or machining.
closedLoop: The encoder returns to its own CL57T drive. The PC receives commanded position, not independent table position; a loose coupler can still escape encoder detection.
axisNote: Four motors, three logical axes. Y-left and Y-right share logical Y; Y-right is not a rotary fourth axis.
labelNote: Source cable IDs come from the corrected cable schedule. Functional-route labels describe additional views and are not new approved harness IDs. Interface labels are planned functions, not proven terminal markings.
viewNote: Functional endpoints only. No drawing order, wire color or GPIO name identifies a physical cavity. The actual mating view and continuity remain to be recorded.

holds.label: Socket view unverified
holds.reason: The actual v1.1 board socket view, cable attachment and STEP/DIR/GND continuity have not been recorded. The 18-contact socket must be identified by function; GPIO names do not give physical cavity positions. No installed adapter is assumed.

holds.label: Header view unverified
holds.reason: Record the actual STOP or EXP2 mating view, key direction and signal/GND continuity. Do not count cavities from a generic picture.

holds.label: Drive terminals unverified
holds.reason: Confirm all four drive labels say CL57T V4.1. Record the actual P1–P4 terminal face, keying and mating view before inserting contacts.

holds.label: Command interface unfinished
holds.reason: The planned interface terminals and protected 5 V supply are not physically qualified. Record S3=5V and prove loaded PUL/DIR current, timing and power-up/down behavior. ENA stays unconnected.

holds.label: Alarm circuit unfinished
holds.reason: Each ALM/COMO pair needs its own isolated, current-limited conditioner. Actual polarity and healthy/alarm/open-cable/power-loss behavior are unknown. Healthy-open outputs need added supervision; inversion alone is insufficient.

holds.label: Module circuit unknown
holds.reason: A TLP281 or HW-399 label does not prove terminals, supplies or isolation. Trace any chosen module, including shared pullups; leaving output VCC floating is not an approved recipe.

holds.label: Return path unverified
holds.reason: Record the controller-side return, control-0V/PE reference and any USB/earthed-PC path. Never remove protective earth to force an open reading.

holds.label: Motor harness untraced
holds.reason: Match this motor to its drive and trace the supplied cable while deenergized. Phase identities, connector cavities, route length, fit and shielding are not yet recorded; colors are not proof.

holds.label: Encoder harness untraced
holds.reason: Match this encoder to the same motor and drive. Verify the kit cable and all six functions while deenergized. No replacement cavity map or internal galvanic-isolation claim is established.

holds.label: Motion supply unqualified
holds.reason: The recorded supply is 36 V / 10 A. Four-drive load, regeneration, ripple, branch protection, wire ratings and distribution terminals remain unqualified. No fuse value is selected here.

holds.label: Hardware stop not proved
holds.reason: Protective bonding, independent hardware stopping and gravity-loaded Z support remain unproved. ENA is unused; a stopped command stream does not remove torque or prevent movement.

routes.title: X: control cable to CL57T P1

upstream.label: Octopus MOTOR0
upstream.note: Driver socket signals; no plug-in stepper driver. EN is reserved and unconnected.

routes.summary: Two signal pairs tell this drive when to step and which way. The planned interface sits between the Octopus socket and P1.
routes.check: Match the cable label at both ends. Verify PUL and DIR as separate pairs; leave ENA and BRK unconnected.

routes.title: X: socket to interface
routes.summary: These signals come from the empty driver socket. The separate four-pin A1/A2/B1/B2 motor-output plug is unused for this external-drive control cable. The planned interface input names are functional labels until its actual terminals are confirmed.
routes.check: Identify STEP, DIR and logic return on the actual board. Confirm the cable attachment and interface terminal map before landing conductors. Leave reserved EN and unused socket contacts unconnected.

routes.title: X: drive to motor
routes.summary: P3 carries motor phase current. Keep this motor and its encoder paired with the same drive.
routes.check: Trace the matched kit harness with all energy isolated and discharged. Never plug or unplug it while powered.

routes.title: X: motor feedback to drive
routes.summary: The drive reads this encoder locally. P2 VCC supplies the encoder; never feed it from an external 5 V or 24 V supply.
routes.check: Trace all six functions in the matched harness while deenergized. Route it away from motor and bus wiring; do not add ground bonds.

routes.title: X: polarized drive power
routes.summary: P4 is polarized DC power. Each drive gets its own protected pair from the distribution point; no drive-to-drive daisy chain.
routes.check: Confirm markings and trace positive to +VDC, negative to GND with all sources isolated. Supply and protection approval remain open.

routes.title: X: alarm to conditioner
routes.summary: This raw alarm pair goes only to its own isolated, current-limited conditioner. Never chain raw drive alarm transistors into PB1.
routes.check: Record healthy, alarm, cable-open and lost-power behavior with the approved test setup. Never hot-unplug a motor or encoder to force an alarm.

routes.title: X: per-axis fault wiring (not read)
routes.summary: Wiring for a future firmware candidate only. The current firmware never reads PG12, so it neither stops motion nor identifies this drive. PB1 is the only drive-fault stop.
routes.check: Use the separately qualified controller-side indication and return. Leave the STOP header’s 5 V cavity empty.

routes.title: All drives: aggregate fault to PB1
routes.summary: The four drive healthy channels join all required cabinet/spindle fault sources. All required contributors healthy = PB1 low; fault, open cable or lost power must make it high. The combining circuit is still unreleased.
routes.check: Prove every contributor independently using the approved test setup before any coupled dual-Y motion; PB1 is the only drive-fault stop. PB1 is a controller fault input; the independent hardware stop is still required.
routes.otherContributors: Required cabinet/spindle fault sources and their conditioning remain to be established by the reviewed complete circuit.
